key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in neural trial functions preserves accuracy at small viscosity without requiring a grid that resolves the layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training costs for low-viscosity flow simulations by representing thin near-wall vorticity layers analytically rather than through mesh refinement.
method: Build sl-PINN trial functions with a corrector for the √ε-wide vorticity layer.
Tie the corrector amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limit solution.
Use coarse-grid finite-volume Laplacian fluxes in sl-FVNN to reduce residual-evaluation cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform accuracy over six viscosity decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN within random-seed scatter at about half the cost per training step.
watch_item: The reported results concern two-dimensional flows with slip boundary conditions; applicability to other boundary conditions or geometries remains to be established.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
